text.arabic_uthmani: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثَٰثًۭا وَرِءْيًۭا

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a fresh divine historical reply
words.prose: {{ar:و}} ({{tr:wa}}) is not a loose continuation of the boast in 19:73. It resumes the discourse and moves the reader from reported human taunt into a divine counter-narrative, so the following destruction formula arrives as an answer with a changed speaking authority.

topics.headline: resumptive shift into divine reply
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 19:74 does not extend the human boast but interrupts it with a divine historical answer.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar marks the conjunction as resumptive, and the following first-person destruction verb confirms a discourse shift from reported speech to divine assertion.

words.gloss_range: exclamatory quantity functioning as the fronted object of destruction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: partitive generation phrase specifying the class counted by {{ar:كم}} ({{tr:kam}})

words.prose: {{ar:كم}} ({{tr:kam}}) is exclamatory, not a request for a number. By standing before the verb as its object, it makes the sheer multitude of destroyed generations the first pressure in the ayah, and its later specification by {{ar:من قَرْنٍ}} ({{tr:min qarnin}}) keeps the count broad rather than tied to one named people. After the comparative question in 19:73, this word answers competitive ranking with the scale of history.

topics.headline: fronted exclamatory count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices magnitude before agency: the ayah first confronts the boasters with how many have already been destroyed.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the pronoun the explicit object of the destruction verb, while QAC marks it as exclamatory rather than interrogative.

topics.headline: counter-measure to the boast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply changes the measure from social superiority in 19:73 to the abundance of destroyed elites.
topics.reason: The boundary row coheres with the resumptive opening and the exclamatory construction; no guardrail evidence contradicts the rhetorical pairing with 19:73.

words.gloss_range: Form IV causative perfect: We caused destruction, with completed divine agency
words.root_gloss_range: destruction, perishing, and ruin; the local Form IV perfect selects caused destruction by the divine first-person subject

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: fronted exclamatory object governed by the destruction verb
generation noun specifying the counted class

words.prose: {{ar:أَهْلَكْنَا}} ({{tr:ahlaknā}}) makes the collapse active and completed: the Form IV shape and first-person plural ending present destruction as a caused divine act, not as a generation merely fading away. Its object is the preceding {{ar:كم}} ({{tr:kam}}), while {{ar:قَرْنٍ}} ({{tr:qarnin}}) specifies the counted class. The verb also enters a recurring destroyed-generation formula, with the same surah returning to it at 19:98 and related warning patterns naming empowered predecessors (6:6), hypothetical destruction before a messenger (20:134), seeing destroyed peoples (36:31), and stronger peoples (50:36). Because the destruction verb comes before the later superiority clause, annihilation is grammatically decisive before wealth and appearance are even named.

topics.headline: completed caused destruction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the destroyed generations did not merely perish; the morphology names completed divine causation.
topics.reason: QAC and the verb-instance evidence identify a Form IV perfect with divine first-person agency, so the causative reading is locally licensed.

topics.headline: object supplied by the preceding count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb acts on the fronted exclamatory quantity, while the later generation noun explains the counted unit.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:كم}} ({{tr:kam}}) the explicit object and {{ar:من قَرْنٍ}} ({{tr:min qarnin}}) the partitive complement.

topics.headline: recurring historical warning formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this is not an isolated historical claim but a compact entry into a repeated Quranic warning formula.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete formula parallels, including 19:98, 6:6, 20:134, 36:31, and 50:36; contextual evidence supports ordinary h-l-k deployment with divine agency.

topics.headline: destruction precedes prestige
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict of destruction is already in place before the ayah concedes the destroyed peoples' worldly superiority.
topics.reason: Local clause order puts the perfect destruction verb in the main clause before the nominal description of superior possessions and appearance.

words.gloss_range: before them; temporal adverb with a plural suffix aimed at the prior boasters
words.root_gloss_range: frontness, facing, priorness, and receiving; the local adverbial form selects temporal before-ness with a targeted suffix
words.prose: {{ar:قَبْلَهُمْ}} ({{tr:qablahum}}) attaches the warning to the people just in view: the destroyed generations were before them, not merely before someone in abstract history. The bound suffix points back to the boasters of 19:73, while the temporal root field makes the past stand in front of the present as precedent. In related warning patterns, the before-language can mark urgency before punishment (39:55) or stronger destroyed peoples before a later figure (28:78), but here it targets the current social comparison.

topics.headline: before-them as targeted precedent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the past is grammatically aimed at the present boasters through the suffix.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word an adverbial to the destruction verb and the suffix a forced genitive possessor, matching the CRITICAL claim about targeted chronology.

topics.headline: past placed before the boasters
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a spatial pressure in the timing word: the past is made to confront the present, while the local sense remains temporal.
topics.reason: The q-b-l field allows front-facing imagery, but QAC and attachment evidence require an adverbial temporal reading here.

topics.headline: recurring before-destruction pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word belongs to a repeated warning idiom where present confidence is judged against what came before.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete echoes and contrasts, including 19:98, 19:7, 28:78, and 39:55; these support formulaic pressure without overriding the local adverbial parse.

words.gloss_range: partitive or explicative preposition specifying the class counted by the exclamatory quantity

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: exclamatory quantity specified by the following partitive phrase
generation noun introduced as the counted class

words.prose: {{ar:من}} ({{tr:min}}) keeps the phrase bound to {{ar:كم}} ({{tr:kam}}). It introduces {{ar:قَرْنٍ}} ({{tr:qarnin}}) as the class being counted, so the exclamation first gives magnitude and divine agency, then breaks that mass into generation after generation.

topics.headline: class specified after magnitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition turns a vast exclamation into individually countable destroyed generations without naming a single nation.
topics.reason: Attachment and translation-support evidence both treat {{ar:من قَرْنٍ}} ({{tr:min qarnin}}) as the dependent partitive complement of the exclamatory pronoun.

words.gloss_range: an indefinite generation or joined cohort, functioning as the specified unit under the exclamatory count
words.root_gloss_range: joining, coupling, companionship, and generation; the local noun selects a contemporaneous cohort, not recitation or an unrelated q-r-ʾ derivation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: exclamatory quantity multiplying the generation unit

words.prose: {{ar:قَرْنٍ}} ({{tr:qarnin}}) names the counted unit: not an identified nation, but any whole generation joined by one time. Its singular indefiniteness lets each cohort stand as one complete case while {{ar:كم}} ({{tr:kam}}) multiplies those cases beyond ordinary counting. The root's joining field supports the cohort sense here, while disputed q-r-n or q-r-ʾ material does not change the local word. In the wider warning formula, the same generation unit can be described by power (50:36), failed cries (38:3), or surah-internal return (19:98); here the formula targets possessions and visible appearance.

topics.headline: one unnamed generation per instance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning does not name one people; it makes every complete generation a possible instance under the exclamatory count.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as an indefinite singular specification, and attachment evidence makes it the complement that specifies the class counted by {{ar:كم}} ({{tr:kam}}).

topics.headline: generation as joined cohort
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the generation as a time-bound cohort destroyed together, while unrelated derivational disputes are kept outside the local sense.
topics.reason: The aligned root is q-r-n and the local noun is the generation word; broader attachment-family senses can color the cohort idea but do not redirect it into Qur'an-derivation debates.

topics.headline: shared unit across warning formulas
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same generation unit carries different historical warning variants, making 19:74 a prestige-focused version of a larger formula.
topics.reason: Rows cite concrete parallels at 19:98, 38:3, and 50:36, and the local formula keeps the shared unit while varying the trait under judgment.

topics.headline: assembly contest widened into history
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from one social boast in 19:73 to an entire panorama of generations.
topics.reason: The boundary claim is supported by the prior ayah's social contest and the local move to an indefinite generation unit.

words.gloss_range: independent plural pronoun resuming the destroyed generation as subject of the nominal clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: plural suffix pointing to the present boasters

words.prose: {{ar:هم}} ({{tr:hum}}) resumes the indefinite generation as a definite group and starts the copula-less nominal clause. It keeps two plural chains apart: the suffix in {{ar:قَبْلَهُمْ}} ({{tr:qablahum}}) points to the present boasters, while this independent pronoun points to the destroyed predecessors. The grammar therefore states their superiority as a flat fact even though the main verb has already announced their destruction.

topics.headline: destroyed group made definite
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that an unnamed generation becomes a definite group whose excellence is stated directly.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the pronoun as the subject of the nominal clause whose predicate is {{ar:أَحْسَنُ}} ({{tr:aḥsanu}}).

topics.headline: boasters and predecessors kept distinct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah compares two groups without letting the repeated plural pronouns blur them together.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix in {{ar:قَبْلَهُمْ}} ({{tr:qablahum}}) and the independent subject pronoun have different local functions, preserving the comparison.

words.gloss_range: better or more excellent, locally confined to the domains specified by furnishings and visible appearance
words.root_gloss_range: goodness, beauty, excellence, and doing well; the local elative is narrowed by the two accusative specifications to worldly prestige markers

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: furnishings as the first worldly domain of superiority
visible appearance as the second worldly domain of superiority

words.prose: {{ar:أَحْسَنُ}} ({{tr:aḥsanu}}) concedes real superiority, but confines it to the prestige fields named by {{ar:أَثَاثًۭا}} ({{tr:athāthan}}) and {{ar:رِئْيًا}} ({{tr:riʾyan}}). The copula-less clause states that superiority without softening it into a merely past report; the irony is that better worldly standing belongs to people already destroyed. The same comparative measure answers the boast of 19:73, while contrasts such as 2:195 and 37:105 show how moral goodness differs from this materially specified excellence. The wider warning field also contrasts stronger predecessors in 28:78 and perceived goodness overturned by judgment in 35:8.

topics.headline: superiority stated without past copula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah grants the destroyed peoples' superiority as a direct fact, which sharpens rather than weakens the warning.
topics.reason: The attachment profile marks {{ar:أَحْسَنُ}} ({{tr:aḥsanu}}) as the predicate of {{ar:هم}} ({{tr:hum}}), and the local clause lacks a past copula.

topics.headline: goodness confined to prestige markers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the h-s-n evaluation is real but restricted to possessions and appearance, not moral rank.
topics.reason: The two accusative specifications define the respect in which the comparative is true, narrowing broad h-s-n goodness to worldly markers.

topics.headline: boast vocabulary redirected
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine reply takes the boasters' own comparative vocabulary from 19:73 and turns it against them.
topics.reason: The rows establish the repeated elative from 19:73 to 19:74, and the suffix in {{ar:قَبْلَهُمْ}} ({{tr:qablahum}}) supplies the comparison target.

topics.headline: worldly comparative warning field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah belongs to a field where what appears excellent or stronger is exposed by judgment.
topics.reason: The cited comparisons at 28:78 and 35:8 are valid contrasts for comparative worldly valuation, while the local syntax remains governed by the two tamyiz nouns.

words.gloss_range: household furnishings and goods as the first accusative specification of superiority
words.root_gloss_range: fullness, abundance, and furnishings; the local noun selects concrete domestic goods, with geminated sound reinforcing density

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: comparative adjective governed by the furnishings specification

words.prose: {{ar:أَثَاثًۭا}} ({{tr:athāthan}}) is not generic wealth. As an indefinite accusative specification after {{ar:أَحْسَنُ}} ({{tr:aḥsanu}}), it names the domain of superiority as household goods and furnished domestic plenty. Its rarity, concrete household sense, and doubled root sound make the wealth almost tangible. The only listed parallel at 16:80 places such goods in a provision context, while 19:74 places them inside a destruction reply; the near-repeat at 19:98 strips these material nouns away, making this occurrence the fuller prestige version, and 50:36 shows the same destroyed-generation formula can replace wealth with sheer power.

topics.headline: furnishings specify the comparison
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices exactly where the destroyed generations excelled: in furnished possessions, not moral worth.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as the first accusative specification governed by {{ar:أَحْسَنُ}} ({{tr:aḥsanu}}).

topics.headline: concrete domestic abundance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply reaches into settled household comfort rather than only public resources or abstract wealth.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows and QAC grammar converge on rare concrete household goods, while the missing V4 root means no dictionary branch should be added beyond the supplied evidence.

topics.headline: doubled sound and fullness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a sound-semantic density: the doubled consonantal shape reinforces the heavy plenty the word names.
topics.reason: The geminated root and supplied semantics both point toward fullness; this is a phonological payoff, not a separate lexical sense.

topics.headline: furnishings fail as protection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that household plenty can appear as provision in 16:80 but becomes no shield in the destruction setting of 19:74 and is absent from the stripped echo at 19:98.
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete references, especially 16:80 and 19:98, and the local destruction clause confirms the failed-protection contrast.

words.gloss_range: and visible appearance or outward condition, the second accusative specification of superiority
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, perceiving, appearing, and visible state; the local rare noun selects outward appearance, with variant evidence kept as apparatus

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: comparative adjective governing the appearance specification

words.prose: {{ar:وَرِءْيًۭا}} ({{tr:wa-riʾyan}}) adds the public-facing half of the prestige field. It is the second accusative specification under {{ar:أَحْسَنُ}} ({{tr:aḥsanu}}), coordinated with furnishings, so the ayah pairs interior goods with exterior appearance. A common seeing-root appears in a rare noun for being seen, and the ayah closes on that visible status after destruction has already been declared. Variant forms sharpen the apparatus: ostentation, attire, metathesis, and hamza smoothing are possible contrasts, but the local canonical word remains outward appearance. The word also bridges backward to vision-warning formulas such as 36:31, contrasts with dream-vision in 12:4 and perceived goodness in 35:8, and points forward to the seeing verb in 19:75.

topics.headline: appearance as coequal comparison domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison covers not only private goods but also public visible condition.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word both coordinated with furnishings and an accusative specification under {{ar:أَحْسَنُ}} ({{tr:aḥsanu}}).

topics.headline: common seeing root made conspicuous
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the familiar seeing-root turned into a rare noun for social visibility.
topics.reason: The contextual evidence shows a rare nominal profile against abundant r-ʾ-y usage, while the local QAC tag confirms a noun of outward condition.

topics.headline: variants color the display field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final appearance word is form-sensitive, while the canonical reading remains outward visible state.
topics.reason: The variant rows are useful as apparatus and contrast, but they do not replace the canonical local parse of {{ar:وَرِءْيًۭا}} ({{tr:wa-riʾyan}}) as appearance.

topics.headline: appearance closes the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends on visible prestige precisely after showing that visibility did not protect its owners.
topics.reason: The word is the final lexical item of the ayah and belongs to the nominal superiority clause that follows the completed destruction verb.

topics.headline: from seeing lessons to being seen
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a visual reversal: other formulas ask people to see destroyed generations, while this ayah names the destroyed people's own visible show.
topics.reason: The rows cite concrete visual contrasts at 12:4, 35:8, and 36:31 and the immediate forward bridge to 19:75; these remain echoes rather than local sense replacements.

topics.headline: public boast answered by public display vocabulary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prior public assembly boast in 19:73 is answered with a word for outward display.
topics.reason: The boundary row coheres with the local coordination of possessions and appearance as prestige domains after the 19:73 boast.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The destroyed earlier qarn is explicitly granted comparative superiority in furnishings and visible appearance.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah concedes the strongest visible status evidence and places annihilation over it; the point is not that the former people lacked splendor, but that splendor had no preserving force.

activation_trace.role: Annihilation supplies the terminal operation that cancels the cohort's apparent advantage.
A people joined in one time supplies the social unit whose status is tested.
Desirable beauty supplies the conceded comparative rather than a sarcastic denial of it.
Abundant household goods supply the material half of the superiority claim.
Visible aspect and appearance supply the inspectable half of the claim.

changed_reading.before: Earlier richer and better-looking peoples were also destroyed.
changed_reading.after: The ayah puts the best available status evidence under cross-examination: it grants material and visual superiority, then demonstrates that the granted advantage cannot preserve its bearers.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Qarn, dense athath, and mutually visible ri'y can be read as one assembled social-material display.
baseline_models.mechanism: Binding, density, and visibility make superiority relational: goods, bodies, and peers must be gathered into an arrangement before they can register as status.

activation_trace.role: Binding one thing to another supplies the cohort as an assembled rather than merely counted unit.
Dense accumulation supplies the packed material texture of the display.
Mutual facing and visibility supply the audience relation through which the arrangement becomes comparative.

changed_reading.before: A generation possessed finer furniture and looked better.
changed_reading.after: Its advantage was a bundled social-material arrangement whose density and mutual visibility made it legible as public rank.

context_deltas.mechanism: The qarn becomes one occupancy in a replacement chain: a successor takes a predecessor's place, while inheritance language relocates durable acquisition away from a cohort's self-secured splendor.

activation_trace.role: Temporal precedence locates the splendid cohort as an earlier station in a sequence.
The time-joined people supply one replaceable cohort in that sequence.
A thing coming after and standing in another's place supplies explicit successor substitution.
After opposed to before supplies the directional link between predecessor and successor.
Transfer from predecessor to inheritor supplies an alternative account of what can pass beyond one cohort.

structural_cues: 19:59 places a successor after predecessors, while 19:74 looks before the present audience to an earlier qarn.
19:63 introduces inheritance before 19:74 displays possessions that failed to preserve their holders.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies succession, before/after, inheritance, and a destroyed cohort; I infer that worldly superiority is temporary occupancy rather than secured ownership. A live alternative is that the inheritance language concerns a separate promised domain and only loosely reframes the historical comparison.

changed_reading.before: The verse gives a static example of a former generation's fall.
changed_reading.after: The former generation occupies a transferable historical slot: successors may inherit position and display, but no cohort can convert that temporary occupancy into permanence.

context_deltas.mechanism: Visible prestige is only the first sight in a delayed epistemic sequence: a promise hidden from present eyes comes, is eventually seen, and overturns the verdict drawn from present appearance.

activation_trace.role: Present visible appearance supplies the initial basis of comparison.
Concealment from eyes supplies the presently unavailable side of the evaluation.
Coming and arrival give the hidden promise temporal movement toward disclosure.
Actual seeing supplies the later observation that replaces the status-bearing first view.
A promise bounded by an appointed time or place connects deferred disclosure to what had been unseen.

structural_cues: 19:61 joins the unseen to a promise characterized as coming.
19:74 names superior visible appearance; 19:75 then uses seeing after an extension marked by 'until when'.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hidden promise, arrival, present appearance, and later seeing; I infer a two-sight reversal in which the later view judges the earlier one. The alternative is a simpler warning in which the repeated seeing vocabulary is not a designed epistemic sequence.

changed_reading.before: Historical destruction proves that attractive appearance is unreliable.
changed_reading.after: The ayah marks present appearance as a provisional first frame: the hidden outcome advances toward a second seeing that will reverse the comparison.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding boast stages rank through a better station and finer council; the focus ayah mirrors its comparative and answers with earlier communities whose even stronger material-visual staging still ended.

activation_trace.role: Many goods supply the material apparatus that answers the prior claim of superior station.
Performance for human observers supplies the socially displayed edge of the focus comparison.
Station and residence supply the setting in which rank is claimed.
The repeated desirable comparative directly links the boast to the counterexample.
The assembled council supplies the peer audience that makes status publicly legible.

structural_cues: 19:73 asks which of two parties is better in station and finer in council.
19:74 is adjacent, retains the comparative 'better,' and escalates from the present parties to many destroyed cohorts.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, repeated comparative language, station, council, furnishings, and appearance; I infer that 19:74 is a mirrored rebuttal using the boasters' own metric. The alternative is a general historical warning with no special claim about status performance.

changed_reading.before: The verse generally warns rich people by recalling richer predecessors.
changed_reading.after: It is a targeted reply to a public prestige argument: the council's visible ranking apparatus is granted, scaled up historically, and shown unable to certify the winning party.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah replaces accumulated appearance with persistence and return: what survives and what comes back to its doer become the counter-metric to goods whose owners undergo annihilation.

activation_trace.role: Annihilation supplies the failure condition against which durability is measured.
Abundant possessions supply the impressive but non-preserving asset class.
Continuance and remaining supply the explicit durability criterion.
A deed's recompense returning to its doer supplies value measured by consequential return.
Return to a place or state supplies the terminal horizon against which present display is valued.

structural_cues: 19:76 twice uses a better-than comparison after 19:74's 'better' furnishings and appearance.
The later comparison explicitly joins remaining deeds to reward and return.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies annihilation, abundant goods, remaining deeds, recompense, and return; I infer that 19:76 supplies the durability test implicit in 19:74. The alternative is that the two comparisons are parallel exhortations without a shared metric.

changed_reading.before: The verse says worldly splendor eventually disappears.
changed_reading.after: The verse participates in a value audit: superiority is not what accumulates or photographs well, but what remains through annihilation and returns as consequence.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it combines a secondary supplied mapping for ri'y with branch-distant ecological images of halaka and athath. It remains anchored at focus words 2, 8, and 9 and the packet explicitly supplies thirst/saturation, dense growth, and rainless barrenness; downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy, not as the lexical sense of the clause.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Athath can image dense growth, the secondary r-w-y mapping can image saturation, and halaka can image rainless barrenness.

activation_trace.role: Rainless barren land supplies desiccation as an exploratory material image of destruction.
Thick, tangled growth supplies lush density beneath the furnishing term.
Satiation opposed to thirst supplies fullness beneath the packet's secondary root mapping.

changed_reading.before: The predecessors had more possessions and a finer outward look.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, their superiority forms a lush, saturated surface whose destruction can be felt as desiccation: visible fullness is a condition, not a guarantee.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates qarn's binding image rather than taking only its ordinary cohort sense. It remains valid as a cross-domain model because the focus binds qarn to dense display and the nearby packet supplies compelled gathering followed by extraction from each faction; downstream prose should say 'as if assembled and unbound,' not redefine qarn literally.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The qarn's supplied binding branch and athath's density allow the prestigious cohort to register as a packed formation.

activation_trace.role: Binding one thing to another supplies the cohort's exploratory assembled texture.
Dense accumulation supplies the packed surface of that formation.
Driving and gathering a group to one destination supplies compelled reassembly.
Pulling a thing from its settled place supplies disassembly by extraction.
A mutually supporting faction supplies the collective from which an element is pulled.

changed_reading.before: A historically earlier generation with dense wealth was destroyed.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, prestige is a packed cohort-display that can be gathered, opened, and plucked apart; its impressive cohesion is itself temporary.

strongest_changes: The focus comparison becomes a mirrored rebuttal to 19:73's public claim of better station and council.
Present ri'y becomes the first frame of a hidden-to-arriving-to-seen sequence whose later sight reverses the verdict.
19:76 supplies persistence and consequential return as the counter-metric to abundant but non-preserving display.
summary.what_was_special: The trace links social staging, temporal disclosure, and durability without denying the predecessors' actual splendor; the packet's split mapping for ri'y also preserves a contained saturation/desiccation outlier.
remaining_uncertainties: The r-w-y saturation reading is explicitly exploratory and should not displace the dominant r-hamza-y appearance reading.
The succession/inheritance model depends on treating nearby transfer language as a reframing of cohort possession rather than a separate promised domain.
The binding/plucking model is mechanism-level imagery, not a claim that qarn literally means an assembled object here.

baseline.text: Onlardan önce nice nesilleri yok ettik; onlar eşya ve görünüş bakımından daha güzeldiler.

findings.text: Önceki kuşakların daha güzel eşya ve görünüşe gerçekten sahip olması reddedilmez; reddedilen, bu görünüşten kalıcılık sonucu çıkarılmasıdır.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Near-verbatim precedent: earlier generations were destroyed despite their apparent ability to call for escape.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: States the same historical proof: destroyed generations do not return, overturning confidence in present display.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Qualifies the destruction motif by locating communal ruin outside a community actively committed to reform.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The surah's closing echo makes 19:74 concrete: those once present leave neither person nor sound.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Immediate antecedent: the disbelievers claim superior gathering-place and social display, which 19:74 answers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Seeing one's effort does not materially illuminate the fate of prosperous earlier generations.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A stronger generation's power and movement through lands did not give it an escape, closely reinforcing the warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Immediate continuation reverses their status comparison when the promised punishment or Hour is seen.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Self-sufficiency helps explain pride, but not the historical destruction or material comparison in the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Supplies the recurring pattern of towns overtaken by divine punishment, though without the display contrast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adam's lapse and lack of resolve do not add a useful neighbor relation here.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Raises the question of the former generations, but contributes no answer to 19:74's warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Especially apt counterexample: generations given greater establishment, rain, and rivers were destroyed for sin.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Immediate resolution: enduring righteous deeds are better in reward and return than the contested worldly advantages.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names an early destroyed people, extending the focus ayah's plural historical precedent.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Links destruction of generations to God's knowledge and sight of servants' sins.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Within the same surah, prior nonexistence challenges human presumptions of secure, self-sustaining status.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Frames ruined towns as a consequence of wrongdoing with an appointed time, sharpening the warning's moral force.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Prophets among earlier peoples supplies broad historical setting but no direct wealth or destruction comparison.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Makes former destruction visible through surviving dwellings, turning past generations into a present sign.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The destruction of defiantly sinful people is related but its exhortation to patience adds little here.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The comparison of God's coloring does not clarify worldly furnishings or destroyed generations.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The unique naming of Yahya has no meaningful relation to the focus contrast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Describes human corruption that destroys cultivation and progeny, not the fate of affluent prior generations.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its mention of furnishings as temporary provision offers a limited lexical contrast to the focus ayah's furnishings.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Like 32:26, presents walking among former generations' dwellings as evidence against heedless confidence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Places many destroyed peoples and generations in a repeated historical series.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Directly counters claims of superiority: earlier peoples had greater strength and traces yet were seized for sins.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The declaration of divine uniqueness does not add to the focus ayah's historical argument.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Another warning through destruction of like-minded predecessors, but less specific than earlier parallels.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's excellence in creation is not a useful neighbor for the stated worldly-status warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Earlier scriptures as evidence bears only a distant relation to recalling prior generations.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Individual sight of good deeds is not materially connected to worldly adornment or destroyed generations.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The reward for excellent work only indirectly contrasts with the focus ayah's worldly measures.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Jesus's blessedness and devotional duties do not clarify this argument.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Condenses the destruction of the earlier ones into a precedent, though it adds no material-status detail.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The superiority of God's judgment has no sufficiently specific connection here.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Establishes warning before punishment, relevant background but not the focus ayah's comparison.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Records revelation after former generations' destruction as guidance and a means of remembering their fate.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ostentation loosely relates to appearance, but the ayah does not address wealth, generations, or destruction.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Creation from prior nothingness does not materially develop the focus ayah's warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Connects rejection of signs and wrongdoing with the destruction of Pharaoh's people and predecessors.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Joseph's fulfilled vision and family reunion do not add a relevant neighbor relation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Thamud's complete removal is a concise example of the earlier destroyed peoples.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A particular people is destroyed after denial, but the repeated formula is less informative than prior examples.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Loss of hearing, sight, and hearts does not clarify the historical material-status contrast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ishmael's household instruction is not pertinent to the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Regret after seeing punishment supports the seriousness of consequences, but not the prior-generations argument.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Earlier destroyed towns that did not believe provide a precedent relevant to the challengers' disbelief.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The command for knowledge before revelation is completed does not develop the focus warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Destruction after denying two messengers is a generic parallel already well represented above.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Direct material parallel: a town exulting in its livelihood is destroyed and its dwellings largely abandoned.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Zechariah's gesture to his people does not illuminate the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Great kingdom and bliss are too distant from the focus's warning about worldly adornment.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds that destroyed towns had warners, providing procedural context for the historical examples.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Prior denial of signs and Thamud's sign provide background but do not develop the material comparison.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Rejects attributing destruction to time, a related correction but not the focus ayah's central comparison.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Merely notes a later generation after another, with no destruction or status lesson.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Sectarian disagreement and the great day do not usefully explain 19:74.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The clearest wealth parallel: Qarun's self-crediting is refuted by earlier, stronger, more amassed generations destroyed by God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs destruction of an unjust town with replacement by another people, extending the generational pattern.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Past betrayal and God's enabling do not materially illuminate the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: States that every destroyed town has a known decree, giving order to the focus ayah's historical warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The lack of covenant fidelity is too general without a direct link to the focus contrast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Rules for children reaching maturity are unrelated.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Announces destruction of a wrongdoing town, but adds little after stronger destruction examples.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Nearby destroyed towns make the precedent geographically immediate and aim to prompt return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Those once certain of no decline ask for delay when punishment arrives, directly challenging permanence claims.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A universal statement about towns' end is broad and less specific than the focus's prior-generation warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Misleading companions and prior communities offer only a remote thematic relation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: A legal penalty in Joseph's narrative is not a useful neighbor.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Universal perishing under divine judgment gives a broad impermanence frame, but lacks the focus's historical polemic.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Explains that earlier generations were destroyed for wrongdoing after clear messengers came, closely grounding the warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Demanding the share before judgment does not illuminate the material-display claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: More powerful towns were destroyed without a helper, another direct refutation of confidence in communal strength.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The appeal to ancestral association and accountability is only distantly related to former generations.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The cry for destruction in Hell does not address historical destruction or worldly status.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Perishing and living on clear evidence is conceptually related but not a close neighbor of the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Moses's plea after the earthquake is not a useful parallel to the focus argument.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The repeated cry for destruction in Hell adds no relevant clarification.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Fear that grief will destroy Jacob is unrelated to the destroyed prosperous generations.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Directly joins former generations, luxury, corruption, and ruin; it diagnoses attachment to ease behind the warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A rebuke for reacting to the discourse does not add a specific neighbor relation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shows warning persisting even when destruction is expected, supplying ethical context for such precedents.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Best deeds and resurrection disbelief only broadly contrast with evaluating worldly display.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Identifies the present warning with earlier warners, a limited link to historical precedent.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Humiliation of liars on the Last Day is not a meaningful neighbor here.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: A companion in a Paradise dialogue is unrelated.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Noah's open warning is generic background rather than a direct interpretation of the focus ayah.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Explicitly disputes who is better by recalling destroyed criminal predecessors, closely matching the focus's comparative rhetoric.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Earlier peoples rejecting messengers is relevant background but less informative than destruction parallels.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The command to warn an unwarned people adds limited context, not the focus's status reversal.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyin kaybolma, bozulma, ölme veya bütünüyle ortadan kalkma sonucuna varmasını ve geçişli kullanımda başkasının bu sonuca sürüklenmesini açıkça destekler. Korku, yoksulluk ve azap adlandırmaları ile yatağın üzerine düşme kullanımı çekirdek anlamdan ayrı, bağlama bağlı uzantılar olarak tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği gerçekleşmiş yok oluş veya işlev kaybıdır; tehlikeye atılma, yer adı, açgözlülük ve özel kalıplar bu çekirdeğe katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın biçimlerdeki yok olma ve yok etme çekirdeği ile sahibinin elinden çıkma, yiyeceğin bozulması ve yatağa düşme gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımlar ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin kaybolarak, bozularak, ölerek veya bütünüyle ortadan kalkarak varlığını ya da işlevini yitirmesi; geçişli kullanımda bir başkasının bu sonuca sürüklenmesidir. Korku, yoksulluk ve ağır eziyet için söylenmesi ile yatağın üzerine düşme kullanımı bu çekirdeğin bağlama bağlı uzantılarıdır.

facets.statement: Bir şey kaybolma, bozulma, ölüm veya ortadan kalkma sonucunda varlığını ya da işlevini yitirir.
Geçişli kullanımda bir kişi veya güç başka bir şeyi yok oluş ya da ağır bozulma sonucuna sürükler.
Korku, yoksulluk ve ağır eziyet de yol açtıkları yıkım bakımından bu adla anılabilir.
Belirli bir yatak ifadesinde anlam, kişinin yatağın üzerine düşmesidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği, varlığın veya işlevin kayıp, bozulma, ölüm ve yoklukla sona ermesidir. Geçişli kullanım bu sonucu başkasına yöneltir; ağır sıkıntı adlandırmaları ve yatağa düşme örneği ise çekirdeğin özel bağlamlardaki uzantılarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Varlığın ya da işlevin kayıp, bozulma, ölüm veya ortadan kalkmayla sona erdiği çekirdek durum ile bunun başkasına yaptırıldığı geçişli kullanım için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Hem yok oluş sonucunu hem de bir başkasını bu sonuca sürükleme yönünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin, malın veya düzenin ağır bozulma ve yok oluşa uğradığı bağlamlarda doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Ağır bozulma ve yok oluş sonucunu güçlü biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Sahibinin elinden çıkma gibi daha tarafsız kayıp kullanımlarını ve geçişli yönü dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnız kişinin yatak veya döşek üzerine düştüğünü bildiren özel kullanımda geçerlidir.

error_profile.preserves: Özel kullanımın düşme hareketini ve hedef yüzeyi eksiksiz korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hem kişinin kendisini sonu yok oluş olan tehlikeye atmasını hem de sonu böyle bir yok oluşa varan şeyi bildirir. Kuş örneği çekirdeği açıklayan özel bir olaydır; gerçekleşmiş ölüm veya uçurumun kendisi dalın tanımı değildir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Sınır, gerçekleşmiş yok oluşta değil, kişinin kendini ona götüren tehlikeye atmasında ve bu sonucu doğuracak tehlikede kurulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tehlikeli sonucu adlandıran biçimler ile korkan kuşun kendini tehlikeye atmasını bildiren özel ifade ayrılır; anlam yalın yok olma fiiline genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin kendisini ölüm veya ağır yok oluşla sonuçlanabilecek bir tehlikeye atması ve bu sonuca götüren tehlikenin kendisidir. Korkudan kendini tehlikeli bir yere atan kuş, eylemin özel örneğidir.

facets.statement: Kişi kendisini sonu ölüm veya ağır yok oluş olabilecek bir tehlikenin içine atar.
Sonunda yok oluş bulunan şey veya durum, bu sonucu doğuracak tehlike olarak adlandırılır.
Yırtıcıdan korkan bir kuşun kendisini tehlikeli yerlere atması bu eyleme örnek verilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, kişinin kendisini yok oluş ihtimali taşıyan bir duruma atması ile sonu yok oluşa varacak tehlikeyi aynı anlam alanında birleştirir. Korkan kuş örneği, korunma çabasının bizzat başka bir tehlikeye girişe dönüşebildiğini gösterir.

concept_gloss.text: kendini ölümcül tehlikeye atma ve buna götüren tehlike
concept_gloss.applicability: Hem kişinin kendi eylemini hem de eylemin sonunda yok oluş doğurabilecek tehlikeli durum veya şeyi birlikte temsil eder.

error_profile.preserves: Eyleyen kişinin kendini tehlikeye atmasını, tehlikenin ölümcül sonucunu ve sonuç doğuran şeyi birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin ağır sonucu bile bile ya da korkuyla göze aldığı tehlikeli girişimler için doğal bir anlatımdır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin kendi eylemiyle ciddi tehlikeye girmesini güçlü biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Tehlikeli şeyin kendisini adlandıran sonuç odaklı yönü dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.collision: Gerçek ateş sanılmaması için bağlam gerektirebilir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal riskli giriş ve ona yol açan tehlikedir; komşu dal ise bu zincirin gerçekleşmiş yok oluş sonucudur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi salınarak ve kırıtılarak yürüme hareketini doğrular, fakat kadın için kullanılan ağır ahlaki niteleme bu hareketin zorunlu anlamı değil, eski ve küçültücü bir değerlendirme uzantısıdır. Tanım hareket çekirdeğini öncelemeli, değer yargısını ayrı bir kullanım olarak göstermelidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal kadın yürüyüşündeki salınma ve kırıtmayı temel alır; ahlaki yargı tarihsel bir niteleme olarak ayrılır ve genel yok oluş anlamı dışarıda kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yürüyüşü bildiren ifade hareketi anlatır; kadın için kullanılan ad ise hareketle ilişkilendirilmiş eski bir küçültücü nitelemedir ve ikisi tek yargıda eritilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kadının yürürken veya cilveli davranırken bedenini salındırıp kırıtmasıdır. Bu harekete bağlanan kadın adı, bazı eski kullanımlarda ayrıca ağır ve küçültücü bir ahlak yargısı taşır.

facets.statement: Kadın yürürken veya cilveli davranırken bedenini salındırır ve kırıtılmış hareketler yapar.
Hareket biçiminden türeyen kadın nitelemesi eski kullanımda küçültücü bir ahlak yargısına dönüşebilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak hareket görüntüsü, yürürken salınan ve kırıtılan bedendir. Bazı açıklamalar bu görüntüyü doğrudan yürüyüş ve cilveyle verirken bazıları kadın için ağır bir ahlaki nitelemeye dönüştürür; ikinci yön çekirdeğin değerlendirme uzantısıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Kadına bağlanan hareket çekirdeğini, yani yürüyüş veya cilve sırasında bedenin salınmasını ve kırıtılmasını doğal biçimde karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Hareketin salınma, kırıtma ve yürüyüş bağlamlarını birlikte korur.

error_profile.preserves: Yürüyüşteki cilveli salınma ve kırıtma hareketini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kadın yürüyüşündeki salınmayı ve bundan doğan küçültücü kadın adını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, süslenip kıvrılmanın yanında kişinin bir ihtiyacı için yumuşak davranıp yalvarmasını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da kadın hareketindeki cilve, kıvrılma ve kırıtma görünümünde örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak yürüyüş ve ona bağlanan kadın nitelemesiyle sınırlıdır; komşu ise istekte bulunurken takınılan yumuşak ve yalvaran davranışa da uzanır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dalda kadın, cilve ve kırıtma bileşenleri ile değerlendirme uzantısı bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal kadınla sınırlı değildir ve atın ya da erkeğin genel olarak sallanarak veya gösterişli yürümesini kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalın gözlenebilir ortak alanı yürüyüş sırasında bedenin yana doğru salınmasıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu genel bir yürüme biçimidir; odak ise kadın yürüyüşündeki cilveli kırıtmayı ve buna bağlanan özel nitelemeyi taşır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal yürüyüşü ve eski küçültücü kadın adlandırmasını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal hareketi özellikle kadının eşine karşı nazlanıp kırıtmasıyla sınırlar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da kadının cilveli biçimde kırıtması ortak harekettir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşuda eşe yönelme şarttır; odakta böyle bir muhatap şartı yoktur ve yürüyüş başlı başına yeterlidir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar incelendi; seçilen üçü hareket çekirdeğini genel salınma, eşe yönelen naz ve daha geniş kırıtma davranışından ayırır. Kalanlar beden görünümü, cinsel temas, gerinme veya kökün ilgisiz dallarıdır.

branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يقال رجل هلوك وليس هو مطلق الموت أو الهلاك

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yalnız yoksulluğu değil, kötü durumdaki kişilerin geçim ve korunma için sürekli olarak kendilerine bakacak kişilere veya iyilik sahiplerine yönelmesini anlatır. Bu nedenle tanım, ekonomik durumu ve yinelenen yardım arayışını birlikte korumalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal ölüm veya yok oluşu değil, yoksulluk yüzünden sürekli yardım ve koruyucu arayan kişi ya da topluluğu anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dal, kötü durumdaki yoksulların sürekli yardım veya bakım aramasını anlatır; özel bir söz öbeğinden genel yoksulluk anlamı türetilmez.

concept_map.definition: Kötü geçim koşulları yüzünden kendisine bakacak birini veya insanların yardımını sürekli arayan yoksul kişi ya da topluluktur.

facets.statement: Kişi veya topluluk kötü geçim koşulları ve yoksulluk içindedir.
Bu kişiler kendilerine bakacak birini veya başkalarının yardımını sürekli arar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar kötü durumdaki yoksulları, yalnız maddi eksiklikleriyle değil, geçim ve bakım için insanların iyiliğine tekrar tekrar yönelmeleriyle tanımlar. Tekil kişi ile böyle kişilerden oluşan topluluk aynı çekirdekte birleşir.

concept_gloss.text: geçinmek için sürekli yardım arayan yoksullar
concept_gloss.applicability: Yoksulluk durumunu, başkalarının iyiliğine yönelmeyi ve bunun sürekliliğini birlikte göstermesi gereken genel kullanım için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yoksulluk, yardım arama ve sürekli yönelme bileşenlerinin tümünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tek bir kişinin geçim veya korunma için sürekli bir destekçi aradığı anlatımlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Tekil kişinin yoksulluğunu ve sürekli yardım aramasını birlikte korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: kendisine bakacak birini sürekli arayan yoksul

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kötü durumda olan yoksul insanları ve onların sürekli bakım ya da yardım arayışını gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal insanlarla sınırlı değildir; hayvan ve kuşların yiyecek veya iyilik aramasını da kapsar ve yoksulluk şartı koymaz.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da bir canlı başkasından geçimlik, bakım veya iyilik elde etmeye yönelir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odakta yoksulluk, insan ve sürekli destek arayışı belirleyicidir; komşu daha geniş bir arayıcı sınıfını ve daha genel bir amaç alanını kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal yardım isteyen eylemden çok, yoksulluk içindeki kişi veya topluluğun kalıcı durumunu ve tekrar eden yönelişini adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal herhangi bir kişinin başkalarından bağış isteme eylemini anlatır; yoksulluk veya süreklilik zorunlu değildir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da kişinin ihtiyacını karşılamak üzere başkalarının vereceği şeye yönelmesi vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu bir isteme eylemidir; odak ise kötü koşulların doğurduğu, sürekli yardım arayan kişi veya grup kimliğidir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal yoksulluğa ek olarak başkasının bakım ve iyiliğini sürekli arama davranışını içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yardım arama davranışı olmadan yoksulluk, ihtiyaç ve muhtaçlık durumunu genel olarak anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da kişinin maddi yetersizlik ve ihtiyaç içinde bulunması ortaktır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu durum adıdır; odak bu duruma başkalarına tekrar tekrar yönelme ve kendine bakacak birini arama bileşenini ekler.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; yayımlananlar yoksulluk durumunu yardım arama eylemi ve yardım arayan kişi kimliğinden ayırır. Diğerleri açlık derecesi, kuruluk, kötü durumun başka görünüşleri veya kökün ayrı dallarıdır.
branches.what_is_ar: الهلاك والصعاليك الذين يطلبون معروف الناس ومن يهتلك إلى من يكفله
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس الهلاك هنا موتا ولا إهلاكا للشيء
branches.source_phrase_ar: المهتلك الذي يهتلك أبدا إلى من يكفله وناس مهتلكون وهلاك (maqayis)؛ الهلاك الصعاليك الذين ينتابون الناس طلبا لمعروفهم من سوء الحال (ayn;tahdhib)؛ الأرامل والهلاك يعني به الفقراء (sihah)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kurak ve boş toprağı, uzun süre yağış almamış araziyi, çetin yılı ve yağmur bırakmadan dağılan bulutu aynı dalda toplar. Bunlar tek bir nesne türü değildir; yağışsızlık ve verimsizlik çevresinde birleşen ayrı kullanımlar olarak tanımlanmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yağışsızlık ve verimsizlik alanındadır; yolcuyu öldüren çöl, dağlar arasındaki uçurum ve kişinin kendini tehlikeye atması bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Araziyi niteleyen söz öbekleri ile çetin yıl adı ayrı tutulur; yağmur bırakmayan bulut da ilişkili bir kullanım olarak gösterilir ve bunlardan yalın bir yok olma anlamı çıkarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Uzun süre yağış almamış, bitkisi ya da ürünü bulunmayan kurak araziyi ve buna bağlı çetin yılı anlatır. Yağmur bırakmadan dağılan bulut da yağışsızlık sonucuyla ilişkili özel bir kullanımdır.

facets.statement: Arazi uzun süre yağış almamış, kurumuş ve bitki ya da ürün bakımından boş kalmıştır.
Kuraklığın belirlediği çetin ve kıtlık içindeki yıl aynı anlam alanında adlandırılır.
Yağmur bırakacakmış gibi yönelip sonra yağışsız dağılan bulut da bu adla nitelenir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, yağışsızlık ve ondan doğan verimsizliği arazi üzerinde merkezileştirir; çetin yıl bu durumun zaman boyutundaki uzantısıdır. Yağmur bırakmadan dağılan bulut ise beklenen suyu vermemesi bakımından aynı alana bağlanır.

concept_gloss.text: kurak arazi, çetin kıtlık yılı veya yağmursuz dağılan bulut
concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın arazi, yıl ve bulut üzerindeki üç ayrı kullanımını yağışsızlık ve verimsizlik ortaklığıyla birlikte temsil eder.

error_profile.preserves: Kurak araziyi, çetin yılı ve yağmur bırakmayan bulutu ayrı ayrı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Uzun süre yağmur görmemiş ve üzerinde bitki ya da ürün kalmamış arazi için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Arazinin yağışsızlığını, kuraklığını ve bitkisizliğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kuraklık ve yokluğun belirlediği ağır bir yılın adlandırıldığı bağlamlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yılın çetinliğini ve kuraklıkla bağlantılı kıtlığı korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: uzun süredir yağış almamış çorak arazi
üzerinde hiçbir şey yetişmeyen kurak arazi

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kurak arazi ve çetin yılın yanında yağmur bırakmadan dağılan bulut kullanımını da içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yağmurun kesilmesini, otlakların azalmasını ve bunun yol açtığı sürekli açlığı daha geniş bir kıtlık zinciri içinde anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da yağış eksikliği toprağın kurumasına, bitkinin azalmasına ve çetin geçim koşullarına yol açar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu neden ve toplumsal sonuç zincirini genişletir; odak belirli arazi ve yıl adlarıyla yağmursuz dağılan bulutu bir araya getirir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal arazi dışında çetin yılı ve yağmur bırakmayan bulutu da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yalnız sulamadan veya yağmurdan pay alamamış araziyi adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalın ortak alanı, suya kavuşmamış ve bu yüzden verimsiz kalmış topraktır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Arazi kullanımlarında güçlü örtüşme vardır; odak dalın yıl ve bulut uzantıları komşuda bulunmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odakta uzun süre yağış almama temel nedendir ve ayrıca çetin yıl ile yağmursuz bulut kullanımları vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dalda bitki yağış kesilmesi dışında yenmiş veya başka biçimde ortadan kalkmış da olabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bitki örtüsünü yitirmiş, verimsiz ve çıplak araziyi kapsayabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu bitkisizliğin sonucuna ve farklı nedenlerine açıktır; odak yağışsızlıkla kurulan kuraklık alanını merkez alır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; seçilen üçü yağışsızlık, bitkisizlik ve kıtlık sınırlarını en açık biçimde gösterir. Diğerleri çıplaklığın farklı nedenleri, belirli yıl adları, değişim belirtileri veya kökün uzak dallarıdır.

branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس المفازة المهلكة من جهة سلوك الطريق ولا المهواة بين الجبلين
